geo_basis: no place stated in the source
date_note: Date is CloudSEK's blog publication day; the page gives no earlier day for the research.
title: CloudSEK: stealer-log credentials from an infected vendor workstation exposed a logistics vendor's portal and data of 40+ enterprise client groups
org: Unnamed corporate transportation and ground logistics vendor
summary: CloudSEK's research team reports that an infostealer infection on a workstation at an external corporate transportation and ground logistics vendor put plaintext administrative portal credentials into a stealer log on a dark web forum. CloudSEK says it reached 18 MS SQL database instances. It says the exposed data covered 40+ enterprise client groups, and gives record counts only as "potentially" up to 4.2 million and up to 1.85 million.
plain: Security firm CloudSEK says one infected computer at a transport vendor leaked login details that exposed data of 40+ of the vendor's corporate client groups. The vendor is not named.
exec: CloudSEK says a single vendor infection exposed 40+ enterprise client groups, showing how supplier credentials leaked in stealer logs can reach customers' data.
action: CloudSEK advises vendors to invalidate exposed credentials and isolate the infected machine, and customers to monitor vendors for leaked credentials and require SSO with MFA for third-party portals.

key_findings: Plaintext admin portal credentials from a stealer log gave access to the vendor's portal
A SQL injection parameter was escalated to remote code execution on the database server
A broken access control flaw in the invoice PDF endpoint let unauthenticated requesters retrieve invoices
recommendations: Invalidate exposed credentials and isolate the infected machine
Require SSO with MFA for third-party portals

evidence.quote: 40+ Major Global Enterprise Client Groups Affected
Potentially Up to 4.2 Million Passenger Movement & GPS Records
Potentially Up to 1.85 Million Downloadable E-Invoice PDFs

validation.note: Only CloudSEK's own research blog read (24 Nov 2026); the vendor and its clients are not named and no second publisher or victim statement was found. Figures are CloudSEK's, and the record counts are hedged with 'potentially'.

review.note: Compared 18 MS SQL instances, 40+ groups, 4.2M and 1.85M with potentially, date, advice against the CloudSEK blog; 40+ is source wording
